payload.markdown: In this chapter, we came to grips with PHP’s advanced object-oriented features. Some of these will become familiar as you work through the book. In particular, I will return frequently to abstract classes, exceptions, and static methods.

blocks.text: In this chapter, we came to grips with PHP’s advanced object-oriented features. Some of these will become familiar as you work through the book. In particular, I will return frequently to abstract classes, exceptions, and static methods.

payload.markdown: In the next chapter, I take a step back from built-in object features and look at classes and functions designed to help you work with objects.

blocks.text: In the next chapter, I take a step back from built-in object features and look at classes and functions designed to help you work with objects.

items: Abstract Classes: A partial base class that forces subclasses to complete certain methods.
Classes & Objects: A class defines state and behaviour; objects are instances of that definition.
Errors & Exceptions: PHP's error and exception system: throw, catch, and the engine's own failures.
Functions: Reusable blocks of code that take arguments and return values.
Static & Constants: Members belonging to the class itself rather than to any one instance.
Arrow Functions: fn() => expressions: closures with automatic by-value capture.
